item.title: Novo, Lilly sputter as Hims launches knockoff GLP-1 pill
item.description: Novo is threatening litigation in response, while FDA head Martin Makary, without naming specific companies, said the agency would take “swift action” against those “mass-marketing illegal copycat drugs.”

item.title: Earnings roundup: AbbVie angst, a bifurcated vaccine market and Bristol Myers’ waiting game
item.description: Vaccine makers are seeing sales declines in the U.S. and upswings in Europe. Elsewhere, investors fretted over an AbbVie franchise and Bristol Myers pointed to a trio of narrative-changing trials.

item.title: Agomab, SpyGlass bank a combined $350M in biotech IPOs
item.description: The two offerings capped off the busiest week for new biotech stock issuances in a year.

item.title: White House’s online service for drug sales debuts with limited impact on prices
item.description: Select products from Pfizer, Eli Lilly and others will be sold at a discount, although the lower costs won’t be felt by many Americans whose medications are covered by insurance.

item.title: Hims cancels plans to sell compounded GLP-1 pill after FDA backlash
item.description: Hims said it “deciding to stop offering access” to the treatment following escalating legal threats — among them a patent infringement suit Novo Nordisk filed against the company on Monday.

item.title: Small and mighty: single-domain antibodies pack a biological punch
item.description: VHH antibodies, they’re not just small, they're modular engineering platforms, capable of powerful biological activity. But with great power comes great challenges!

item.title: Navigating the complexities of Cell and Gene Therapy supply chains
item.description: Turning complex CGT logistics into certainty—keeping therapies moving to patients.

item.title: Takeda, Iambic partner in latest pharma AI push
item.description: “The winners over the next five years” will be the companies that “fully integrate” artificial intelligence into drug development, said Takeda research chief Andy Plump.

item.title: Lilly bets again on China drugs; Roche showcases MS data
item.description: Lilly could pay Innovent Biologics up to $9 billion in a new alliance. Elsewhere, Roche tried to assuage investor concerns about its new multiple sclerosis drug and Roivant shares surged.

item.title: Lilly buys ‘in vivo’ CAR-T maker Orna, extending streak of genetic medicine deals
item.description: Worth up to $2.4 billion, the acquisition is also the latest in a series of buyouts involving startups with technologies that modify immune cells inside the body.
